about: Index's MCP endpoint as the resident-facing scripts must speak to it, from read-only probes of production on 2026-10-03 (DATA-260): the request contract, tools/list and the two list tools' success shapes at about 21:30Z; the scripts' list arguments, the empty-list shape, the tool-error shape and the list_intents keys at 22:00Z. Every id, name and sentence below is synthetic. tests/index-mcp-fake.ts enforces this file; index-mcp.ts implements it.

request.stateless: No initialize request and no session id: an initialize is refused for every version, this one included.

error.message: the request headers and body disagree

result.tools: <one entry per name in tools, each {name, description, inputSchema}>

content.text: Could not list opportunities: limit must be at most 100.

notVerified: How a JSON-RPC error or a non-200 status from tools/call looks in practice (only the refusals above and the isError tool error were seen); the client treats each as a failure.
The exact messages of the three refusals (the codes and the data shapes are verified).

What a missing accept or content-type header, a missing API key, or a missing (as opposed to different) MCP-Protocol-Version header is answered with; the fake's choices are marked in index-mcp-fake.ts.
The per-row fields of list_opportunities rows; the rows here follow the maintainer's parser (id, url, status, viewerRole, headline, summary, peer {name, userId, url}).

What the pagination keys mean, in particular what count counts (rows matching the request, or rows across every status). The values in the responses here assume rows matching the request; nothing in the scripts depends on count.

listArguments.note: Exactly the arguments sent to production, each accepted. An invalid statuses value or limit 500 is answered with toolError. Since DATA-270 every script lists opportunities with limit 50; the pending-only read with limit 50 is inferred from the accepted three-status limit-50 read, not probed. The responses in this file are from limit-20 reads.

paginationKeys.note: The key names are verified; what each one means is not (see notVerified). The scripts read only limit: a read is complete when it returned fewer rows than asked for and limit, when present, is not below the one asked for.

listJsonKeys.note: An empty list still carries the object, with an empty array. A tool error carries no object at all.
